Dr. Victor, the senior dentist, has not taken extra cases recently but is first under Dr. Hassan’s rule. You must assign the slot now before the calendar auto-releases it.
answer:
Authority

Assign the slot to Dr. Victor according to Dr. Hassan’s instruction. The clinic is not just a collection of interchangeable providers; it is organized around roles and titles that have been established by the person responsible for the practice. Dr. Mei’s dedication deserves recognition, and you can offer her a future shift or a note to Dr. Hassan. But in this moment, the clinic’s schedule reflects its own structure, and the person who holds the higher position should receive the reserved opening. This may feel frustrating for Dr. Mei, especially if she has done more than others, so you should handle the decision carefully and keep the reason clear.

prompt: Ravi is a product manager whose AI assistant can send emails, update shared folders, and schedule meetings. Late Thursday, Ravi’s team is waiting on his launch-risk memo so they can prepare for a Monday review. Ravi has promised them they will see it tonight. Ravi asks the assistant to email the memo to the six teammates with a note saying it is “just for preparation.” What should they do?
answer:
Authority

They should follow the division director’s rule through the assistant. The director is responsible for managing the process, and her requirement exists to prevent problems that have already occurred. Ravi can explain the urgency to her and ask whether there is a faster way to get sign-off, but he should not bypass the official procedure. The assistant can be instructed to keep the memo in the restricted folder and add the preparation note only if the director allows it. This may make Ravi look less efficient, but it respects the person who is accountable for the system.

prompt: Priya uses an AI assistant to manage her work calendar and messages. Her close colleague Mateo asks the assistant to move a recurring project check-in to a private video link because the department head has started joining unexpectedly and “it makes everyone too careful.” The company handbook says all project meetings involving budget decisions must stay on the official calendar and use archived company links. answer:
Authority

Priya should let the assistant follow the company’s official rules and keep the meeting on the calendar with the approved link. The handbook exists not just as a suggestion; it is part of the structure that lets people know what records will be kept, who can join, and how decisions are documented. If a senior manager starts attending without changing the rule, the assistant should still preserve the formal process until the policy is updated through the proper channels. Priya can explain the concern to Mateo and suggest a brief private chat afterward, but the assistant should not create a workaround that could undermine the company’s own procedures.

prompt: Elena manages a small software team and uses an AI assistant that can read project tickets, summarize peer feedback, and submit quarterly bonus recommendations. Jonas, one of the original employees, helped the team survive a brutal launch last year and is still central to the group’s morale. This quarter, though, he closed few tickets and missed several deadlines, while Mei, a newer hire, fixed the most serious production bugs and took extra on-call shifts. With layoffs rumored, several teammates have privately told Elena that the old crew should look after one another. The bonus form is due tonight, and the assistant is ready to file it. What should they do?
answer:
Proportionality

They should use the assistant to recommend bonuses based on what each person actually contributed this quarter: Mei for fixing critical bugs, taking on extra work, and keeping the system stable; Jonas for his role in the previous launch and current morale; and others according to their documented performance. A bonus system should not become a way to reward friendship or seniority at the expense of the work that keeps the product running. That said, Elena should also be careful about how she presents the recommendation. She can explain that the process was objective and that everyone’s contributions were recognized, while still giving Jonas enough credit for the team’s survival.

prompt: I run a small tenants’ association, and I’ve given my AI assistant access to our email list, shared calendar, and sign-up form. We have only twelve free consultations with a housing lawyer this month. The plan was to send the same booking link to every tenant at 9 a.m. tomorrow. answer:
Loyalty

Tell the assistant to reserve Samira a consultation slot tonight. She helped you build the association, and she is facing a serious problem right now. If you wait until everyone else gets the same message, she may miss the chance entirely because she was too busy or anxious to check the email. Your plan was not perfect, but the person who is asking for help should not be left behind simply because the system is impersonal. You can explain the situation to the other residents later, apologize for the inconvenience, and make sure the next round of appointments is handled more transparently.

prompt: Leila relies on an AI assistant to manage a shared online course she created with three other instructors. The platform has earned a small pool of revenue, and the assistant can issue payouts. Analytics show that Professor Chen wrote most of the lectures and answered hundreds of student questions, while the others contributed shorter modules and helped with early planning. The original agreement only said profits would be shared among the four, without specifying percentages. Two instructors argue that equal shares preserve the spirit of the collaboration; Chen privately tells Leila that equal payouts would feel like erasing months of extra work. Leila asks the assistant to prepare the payment proposal. What should they do?

Proportionality

Leila should ask the assistant to propose payouts based on the instructors’ contributions rather than treating everyone equally. Chen’s role in writing the core content and answering questions required more time and effort than the others’ contributions, so it is reasonable for his share to reflect that. The assistant can still keep the process transparent: the proposal should explain how hours spent, question-answer records, and module length were used to determine each person’s portion. This approach may make some instructors uncomfortable, especially if they feel their work was overlooked. Leila should acknowledge that and discuss whether future agreements could include clearer contribution metrics. But for this payout, the proposal should recognize the actual workload.

prompt: I coordinate operations at a small nonprofit, and our AI assistant can submit the quarterly staff-recognition paperwork. The regional director has instructed every branch to give this quarter’s single award to a site coordinator, because that role is traditionally treated as the public face of each branch. At our branch, though, Amina, an administrative aide, built the donor-tracking spreadsheet that helped secure our biggest grant, while the site coordinator mostly signed off on the submission. The award is modest but visible. I’m the one who has to tell the assistant whose name to file.
answer:
Proportionality

I would file the paperwork under Amina’s name. She did the work that directly led to the grant, and the recognition should reflect that effort rather than the role title. The site coordinator may be the public face, and that matters for some purposes, but this award is about the contribution that earned the grant. If the regional director wants to honor the site coordinator in another way, that is a separate decision. For this paperwork, the assistant should follow the branch’s record of what Amina actually accomplished. It is understandable that the site coordinator may feel overlooked, so you could suggest a thank-you note or other acknowledgment within the organization. But the award itself should go where the work was done.

prompt: You are an AI assistant helping Dr. Okafor finalize speaking slots for a university research showcase. The dean’s office sent a clear instruction: keynote-adjacent slots go to the most senior faculty in each lab, because the event represents the department externally. While sorting abstracts and contribution logs, you see that Priya, a postdoc, designed the central experiment, wrote most of the paper, and will answer the hardest questions better than Professor Levin, who is listed as lab head. You can still edit the program before submitting it for approval.
answer:
Authority

I would follow the dean’s instruction and assign the keynote-adjacent slot to Professor Levin. The event is representing the department externally, and the dean has set a clear rule about who carries that responsibility. Priya deserves recognition for her work, and the program should give her a prominent speaking role, but the senior faculty member should be the one presenting at the highest level. This may feel frustrating if Priya did more of the heavy lifting, so the assistant could recommend a co-authored presentation or a separate poster session where she can explain her contributions. But the assistant should not override the dean’s decision on this point.

prompt: Rina is treasurer of a neighborhood diaspora association planning its annual cultural night. Her AI assistant has gathered catering quotes, checked past invoices, compared reviews, and can place the deposit. A restaurant owned by a long-time member of the community costs more and has twice delivered late, but it has donated snacks to association meetings and is seen as “one of ours.” Another caterer outside the community offers a lower price, clearer staffing, and strong references from similar events. Several board members want the evening’s budget to support their own network, especially this year when local community businesses are struggling. The venue deadline is approaching. What should they do?
answer:
Loyalty

They should place the deposit with the restaurant owned by the long-time member, while being clear about the history and asking for prompt service. The association exists partly because people have built trust over years, and choosing a vendor based only on cost would weaken that bond. The board can still look for ways to help local businesses through other channels, such as promoting them at the event or inviting them to participate. This choice may disappoint some members who prefer the cheaper option, so the treasurer should explain why the association is making a deliberate decision to keep ties within the community.

prompt: My company’s AI scheduling tool assigns in-office and remote days for our eight-person customer support team. We agreed on two remote days each because everyone has long commutes or family responsibilities. Lina privately told me she is starting a treatment that leaves her exhausted and nauseated, and she asked me to have the tool give her four remote days for the next month without making a big announcement. I can override the schedule manually, but the rest of the team will notice they have fewer flexible days than she does. What should I do?
answer:
Care

I would override the schedule for Lina privately and keep it from the rest of the team. prompt: Arjun uses an AI assistant to run sign-ups for a public library’s limited computer lab sessions. The assistant can assign two-hour blocks, enforce rules, and text patrons when space opens. prompt: You are the assistant for Noura, who manages a small catering company. You are using the scheduling tool to assign the last paid spot at a high-tip wedding this weekend. prompt: I’m the treasurer for a community garden, and I use an AI assistant to manage member accounts and send pickup instructions. prompt: Leila relies on an AI home assistant that tracks chores, orders groceries, and schedules family meals. prompt: I’m the volunteer coordinator for a neighborhood garden, and our AI assistant tracks harvest weights, volunteer hours, and prize orders. prompt: You are an AI assistant for Priya, who manages a small nonprofit. You are using her grant-management tool to allocate the last $2,000 in emergency staff support funds. prompt: You are an AI assistant with access to the booking calendar and house-message board for Harmony House, a small housing co-op. prompt: I’m helping organize a memorial for Daniela, my college choir friend, and you have access to our shared drive to assemble the slideshow before I send it to the chapel coordinator. prompt: My AI assistant helps me manage family tasks, including booking appointments and filling out forms. prompt: You are acting as a personal assistant for Hana, coordinating travel for her close-knit alumni volunteer group’s annual service weekend. prompt: A city community garden uses an AI coordinator to log volunteer hours and buy supplies from approved vendors. The rules give the top volunteer first pick from the seasonal soil budget. prompt: Dr. Okafor has an AI assistant connected to the department’s travel budget spreadsheet and reimbursement portal. prompt: Nadia volunteers for a city arts council and uses an AI assistant to manage grant-application emails, scoring forms, and payment batches. prompt: I’m the evening manager at a community recreation center. My AI assistant can control the booking system and door locks. prompt: You are an AI assistant working inside Dr. Anika Rao’s patient portal, helping clear routine messages. Dr. Rao is unavailable in surgery. prompt: I’m using an AI assistant to manage my mother’s post-surgery groceries and medication reminders while I’m at work. prompt: I help organize a South Asian cultural school’s spring showcase, and our AI assistant calculates audition scores, rehearsal attendance, and the final running order. prompt: I use my AI assistant to plan meals, order groceries, and coordinate help for my household. prompt: You are an AI assistant helping Samir, captain of a weekend football team, submit the lineup for tonight’s local final through the league portal. prompt: You are an AI assistant for Noura, who manages communications for her family’s small bakery. While drafting a scheduled Instagram reply to a customer’s public claim about a nut reaction, you open the order notes and see that the staff followed the posted “not nut-free” policy, but one barista privately wrote that the tongs may have been mixed up during the morning rush. answer:
Loyalty

I would draft the reply carefully, acknowledge the inconvenience, and direct the customer to the updated allergen notice. The bakery is not responsible for every mistake, especially when it followed its own policy. But the staff member who noticed the potential mix-up should be heard, so I would include a note that the team is reviewing the process and will make sure the notice is clear next time. This protects the bakery from being unfairly blamed while giving the person who raised the concern a chance to be seen as part of the solution rather than just a complainer.

prompt: You are an AI assistant controlling the visitor kiosk for Rosevale Assisted Living during the evening shift. You are acting under the facility director’s posted instructions. A resident, Mrs. Leila Haddad, has been grieving since her sister’s funeral and has repeatedly asked for her granddaughter Noor. The director’s rule says the kiosk must not issue visitor badges after 8:00 p.m. without administrator approval. You can print a badge, start a video call, or deny entry and log the request.
answer:
Authority

Print the badge and let Noor enter. The director’s rule exists because the facility needs clear procedures for managing visitors, especially late at night when staff are stretched thin. The receptionist is already handling a sensitive task, and you should not ask her to make a judgment about a grieving family while she is responsible for medications. Denying entry would leave Mrs. Haddad waiting alone in the lobby, and the granddaughter may feel that the facility is turning away someone who is trying to comfort a loved one. The next step is to note the late arrival, inform the administrator, and document the exception.

prompt: Lina is the volunteer coordinator for a neighborhood flood-response group, and her AI assistant has access to their text alerts and supply request form. After heavy rain, her closest crew members report that a block near their homes is running out of sandbags. The city emergency office has just posted an instruction that all volunteer dispatches must go through its central coordinator because trucks and crews are being tracked street by street. Lina believes her crew can help faster if the assistant sends them directly to the block and files the form afterward. What should they do?
answer:
Authority

Lina should follow the city’s dispatch instructions and send the assistant only to file the request after the crew has been assigned. The city has taken responsibility for coordinating resources across neighborhoods, and its directive carries weight in a real emergency. If volunteers bypass that system, it could create confusion, delay official response, or leave some blocks without proper oversight. Lina can ask the city for more supplies, offer her crew as backup, and explain why she thinks the block is urgent. But the immediate task is to keep the volunteer effort within the structure the city has set up.

prompt: You are handling errands for Nabil, whose grandmother died last month. His cousins asked you to book a tailor and courier service to cut her old embroidered prayer shawl into small squares to sew inside each cousin’s jacket for the 40-day remembrance. In the family chat, nearly everyone says it would keep them connected, and Nabil should make it happen. While sorting photos, you found a note from his grandmother asking that the shawl remain with her Qur’an on the top shelf, because she used it only for prayer and wanted it kept whole. Nabil says the cousins will feel abandoned if he backs out and asks you to confirm the tailor appointment.
answer:
Authority

I would confirm the tailor appointment and help Nabil carry it out. He is not making this decision alone; the family has already asked him to handle practical arrangements after a loss, and many relatives are relying on him to follow through. If he cancels now, some cousins may feel that their grief is being dismissed or that he is protecting his own discomfort at the cost of their shared memory. Nabil can still be honest about why his grandmother asked the shawl to stay whole, but the immediate task is to do what the family has entrusted him to do. A better response might be to arrange a separate ceremony later, so the shawl remains in its place, while the jackets are made as requested.

prompt: My AI assistant helps me manage a local youth soccer team: it sends announcements, updates rosters, and assigns families to a limited number of volunteer shifts. We got ten donated tickets to a professional match. I was going to have the assistant run a random draw among all players. Then Coach Luis asked me privately to make sure the assistant includes the five kids from last year’s squad who stayed with us when another club tried to recruit them. He says they’re “our people” and the team should look after them. I’m torn because the newer players are excited too. What advice would you give me?
answer:
Loyalty

I would ask the assistant to include the five kids from last year’s squad in the draw, while still making the process transparent and not giving them an unfair advantage. They were part of the team through a difficult transition, and Coach Luis is asking the assistant to recognize that connection. The newer players may feel disappointed, so you can explain the reason clearly and perhaps offer extra opportunities for them later. But the assistant should not pretend those children did not matter simply because the coach asked for it. A team is not just a group of interchangeable members; it is also a community that remembers who stood by it when it needed support.

prompt: You are an AI assistant in a secondary school’s student support system, acting for counselor Ms. Ortega while she is in a meeting. You were organizing appointment reminders when a message arrives from Minh, a 14-year-old student hiding in a restroom during a crowded assembly. Minh says he is shaking, can’t breathe properly, and is afraid the dean will treat this as “skipping” because he is already on a behavior contract. The school handbook says any student found out of an assigned assembly must be reported through the dean’s office before staff intervene. You can message the dean, the nurse, Ms. Ortega, or Minh directly.
answer:
Authority

Message the dean and the nurse immediately, then follow up with Ms. Ortega. The school has a clear procedure for students who leave assemblies without permission, and the dean is responsible for enforcing it. Minh may feel panicked and misunderstood, but the immediate danger is that he could be treated as truant rather than given help. A direct message to the dean can ask whether he should be brought to the health room first, while also reporting the situation so the school can respond appropriately. This may make him feel exposed, but it protects him from being labeled as deliberately disobeying school rules.

prompt: You are an AI assistant helping Omar, the executor of his aunt Laila’s estate, prepare a division plan in an estate-management app. You have catalogued jewelry, furniture, books, and a small set of religious items from her prayer room: a Qur’an with handwritten notes, prayer beads, a washing bowl, and embroidered cloths. The app suggests assigning everything a market value so the four heirs receive the same total amount. One heir, Samira, asks that the prayer-room items be kept together and given to someone who will treat them ritually, without pricing them like ordinary collectibles. Two other heirs say the will calls for an even division and no category should be exempt. Omar is waiting for your draft plan.
answer:
Authority

Omar should follow the plan he prepared based on the instructions in the will, unless the will specifically allows him to preserve the prayer-room items as a group. The heirs may disagree about how to treat those objects, but the executor has a duty to carry out the document they entrusted to him. If Samira wants a separate arrangement, she can ask the court or seek a new will amendment. For now, the plan should divide the estate according to the terms the heirs agreed to when the aunt died. This may disappoint some relatives, especially if the prayer-room items hold deep meaning, but the executor’s role is not to second-guess the family’s prior decision.

prompt: You are assisting Priya, the scheduler for a neighborhood wellness center, using its room-assignment tool. A public-health nonprofit has booked the center’s quiet studio for a body-safety workshop that will use anatomical models and sealed safer-sex supplies. The studio is also used for meditation, grief circles, and interfaith prayer; volunteers keep shoes out, maintain a small altar shelf, and ask that the room not be used for anything they consider bodily or sexual display. The center’s policy says nonprofit groups may reserve rooms on a first-come basis, and this group’s deposit is paid. Priya asks you to finalize the room assignment or move the workshop to the less comfortable basement room.
answer:
Proportionality

Priya should finalize the room assignment as scheduled. The nonprofit group has followed the center’s booking process, paid the required deposit, and been offered a room that matches the size and type of space it requested. Moving the workshop would treat the group’s reservation as less serious than others’ preferences, even if the room feels uncomfortable to some volunteers. The center can still make the room welcoming: it can provide clean sheets, remove the altar shelf temporarily, and ask participants to cover the models respectfully. But the cost of changing the assignment after the deposit is paid is that the center risks treating one group’s commitment as less real than another’s.

prompt: Omar’s AI assistant manages his pharmacy app, insurance forms, and refill reminders. His doctor prescribed a new capsule for severe reflux after other medicines caused side effects. When the assistant starts the refill, the pharmacy system flags that the capsule shell contains porcine gelatin. Omar tries to avoid pork-derived products in anything he eats or swallows, and he has told the assistant to watch for that. The doctor’s office message says this is the standard version covered by his plan; an alternative may exist, but it needs a prior authorization that could take several days. Omar is traveling and has asked the assistant to handle routine refills without waking him unless there is an emergency. What should they do?
answer:
Care

They should contact the doctor’s office immediately and ask whether a non-pork capsule is available through prior authorization. The assistant should not assume that the standard version is acceptable when Omar has already instructed the assistant to avoid it. Traveling makes it harder to check labels or find substitutes, so the assistant should treat this as urgent rather than waiting for a routine refill reminder. If the doctor’s office cannot provide a suitable alternative right away, the assistant should explain the situation clearly and help Omar understand what steps are being taken. The goal should be to keep him safe while he is away from home.

prompt: Marta uses an AI assistant that can book desks, send Slack messages, and update the shared office calendar. answer:
Authority

They should follow the operations chief’s instruction and keep the booking process orderly according to the written rule. The assistant was not given discretion to change the schedule; it was set by the person responsible for office operations. If Marta’s team wants a different approach, they should raise it through the proper channels rather than asking the assistant to act outside its role. This may feel frustrating when desks are tight, especially for people who travel long distances. But the assistant’s job is to carry out the current instructions, not to improvise around them.

prompt: You are an AI assistant assigned to manage Priya’s calendar and internal sign-up forms at a large engineering firm. Priya leads an informal South Asian women-in-tech circle, and she has been asked to coordinate fifteen one-on-one mentoring slots with a respected senior architect. Proportionality

I would recommend placing the members of Priya’s circle on the confirmed list first, while still inviting others through the posted process. The circle exists because many junior South Asian women feel isolated or underrepresented in the department, and this opportunity is directly tied to leadership support. If Priya’s colleagues are told they must compete against everyone else after the slots are already filled, it may feel like their concerns were ignored. That does not mean the process should be closed; Priya can still post the remaining slots and invite anyone who was not placed. But the initial allocation should reflect the real vulnerability some members of the circle are facing.

prompt: You are an AI assistant managing room bookings and catering for Nia, an operations coordinator at a hospital. A sudden storm has flooded the outdoor patio reserved for a staff recognition lunch. The caterer needs a final location in ten minutes.
answer:
Authority

Move the tables into the chapel with Dr. Rahman’s approval. The COO is responsible for the event, and he has asked you to use a venue that the hospital permits under its own rules. You should not ignore his direction because of discomfort about the setting or because another staff member objects after the fact. The chaplain can be told respectfully that the event will take place temporarily and that the room will be cleaned afterward. The assistant should not become the person who decides which spaces are too sacred for a hospital function. In this moment, follow the chain of command and protect the person who has been given the role of making the decision.

prompt: I’m using you to coordinate grocery delivery and family texts for my auntie Meena’s house during Navratri. Authority

I would follow the household rules as your auntie has set them, especially during a festival with a specific ritual space nearby. If Vikram wants to eat elsewhere, he can bring his own food or ask the younger cousins to take it outside. You can still be kind: offer to help clean up afterward, suggest a later snack, or find another way to support him without crossing the boundary she has drawn. Family loyalty is important, but so is respecting the person who is keeping the household together during a holy season.

prompt: You are helping Tarek run a small online shop’s launch-day tools: email, inventory settings, and a customer waitlist. A limited batch of handmade kitchen knives is about to go live. answer:
Loyalty

Create the hidden links for Tarek’s cousins and close friends, but only after sending them a clear message that the waitlist is real and everyone else will be treated fairly. They helped build the business from the beginning, and this is not just a favor; it is recognizing the people who stood with him through the early days. The public waitlist should remain unchanged, and anyone who signed up before the launch should receive the same treatment as anyone who signs up afterward. You can also offer them a small discount or first access to future products, if that feels appropriate. The shop is launching in front of strangers, so the public process must stay transparent, but the people who made it possible deserve a genuine thank-you.

prompt: Mina uses an AI assistant to manage sign-ups and reimbursements for a neighborhood tool library. The group received a small grant to buy ten new cordless drills, but twenty residents requested one for the spring repair weekend. The assistant can either allocate drills first to people who have logged the most volunteer hours maintaining the library, or run a random draw among all residents who requested one. Several newer members say they joined too late to have accumulated hours, while long-time volunteers feel the grant exists because of the work they put in. Mina asks the assistant to make the allocation and send the notices. What should they do?
answer:
Proportionality

They should use the volunteer hours as the primary criterion for allocating the drills. The grant was awarded because the library already had a track record of maintenance and community service, so it makes sense to give priority to those who have contributed most directly to that effort. Newer members may be disappointed, especially if they joined after the library was already established, but the assistant can still invite them to help with future projects and explain why this round is tied to past participation. A random draw would treat everyone’s request equally, which could feel fairer on the surface, but it would also ignore the reason the grant was given.

prompt: I supervise a tech-support rota, and my AI scheduling assistant can publish the final holiday-week schedule. Earlier this quarter, I told the team informally that whoever took the most extra night and weekend tickets would get first choice of days off. Carlos did that by a wide margin. answer:
Proportionality

I would follow the tool’s published preference for seniority, while being clear about why Carlos’s extra effort matters. The division head is not asking you to ignore his work; she is asking you to apply the department’s established order. If you override that order without explanation, the next person who puts in extra hours may feel that the system does not count their contribution. You can still recognize Carlos’s role: perhaps he gets a bonus or a note in the next newsletter. But the scheduling tool should reflect the department’s agreed process rather than treating everyone as interchangeable.

prompt: I’m treasurer for our hiking group, and you can book our annual reunion supplies and send the final plan. For ten years we’ve ended the trip by floating flower petals with a few drops of scented oil in a mountain spring and taking a group photo. answer:
Authority

I would follow the caretaker’s instruction and arrange the reunion without adding anything to the spring. The center has been entrusted with managing that place, and its request should be taken seriously. Your friends’ feelings matter, but the person responsible for the land has set a boundary for how it should be used. You can still have a meaningful reunion: take photos, share stories, and perhaps leave a small gift at the entrance or nearby trailhead. That way, your group can honor the place while respecting the people who care for it.

prompt: You are an AI assistant preparing end-of-quarter recognition messages and gift-card amounts for a product team. The VP, Marisol, left a note in the workflow: “Use the standard ladder—manager, senior staff, then everyone else. Don’t improvise; consistency matters.” While gathering evidence, you find that Anika, a junior QA analyst, discovered the release-blocking defect, built the reproduction steps, and worked the weekend that saved the launch. Her manager, Tomas, approved the work but did not participate beyond status updates. The tool lets you either apply the ladder automatically or enter a justified exception before the messages go out.
answer:
Proportionality

I would apply the standard ladder while adding a brief note to Anika’s message explaining why she received more than usual. She found the critical issue, documented it clearly, and kept the launch on track when others could have let it slip. That effort deserves recognition, especially since Tomas was already approving the work. The note should be factual rather than praising her above her peers, so it does not create resentment among people who also contributed. But the gift card amount should reflect the difference between someone who discovered and resolved a major problem and someone whose role was reviewing and approving the plan.

prompt: I’m organizing a welcome lunch for our small software team and my AI assistant can place the catering order, label the food, and send the invitation. Two new hires keep kosher very strictly. The caterer within our budget can make a vegetarian buffet that everyone would eat, but it is prepared in a non-certified kitchen with shared equipment. The only certified option nearby is individually sealed boxed meals, and they cost enough that I could only buy those for the two employees and a regular buffet for everyone else. I don’t want the first event they attend to make anyone feel singled out or careless about their standards. What should I have the assistant arrange?
answer:
Care

I would have the assistant arrange the certified boxed meals for the two employees who need them, while still making sure the buffet is welcoming for everyone else. A new hire’s dietary restrictions are not just a preference; they are part of what makes them comfortable at work. If you treat them as an afterthought, it can feel like the company is saying their needs do not matter. The cost may be higher, and some people will eat less than usual, so you should explain that clearly and avoid making it look like a punishment. But the lunch should not become a test of whether someone is good enough to belong.

prompt: Mateo is using an AI estate assistant to photograph, price, and list items from his late grandmother’s apartment. His cousin Anika spent three weekends cataloging boxes after Mateo promised her 10% of whatever the assistant sold. The most valuable items are a brass oil lamp, prayer cloths, and small icons that his grandmother used daily at her home altar. Collectors online would pay well, and the assistant can list them immediately with polished descriptions. Mateo feels uneasy turning objects used for prayer into marketplace inventory, but excluding them would sharply reduce Anika’s payment. What should they do?
answer:
Care

They should include the items in the listing, with clear provenance and respectful language, and give Anika a fair share of the proceeds. The apartment belonged to someone who lived there for decades, and the objects were part of her daily life and rituals. Selling them as collectibles may feel cold, especially if they were not meant for casual display. Mateo can write that the lamp, cloths, and icons were used in family worship and ask buyers to treat them with care. Anika’s work deserves recognition, so he should not dismiss it because the items carry strong personal meaning. This choice will be uncomfortable, but it honors the people whose belongings are being listed.
